doc.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023

title: Smoky clubs and quitting smoking
summary: He smoked after joining the Navy, felt a warning ping and quit about 40 years ago.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Was there a difference in playing in formerly smoky nightclubs than when they weren’t later?

With Stan and Woody we did some nightclubs. We didn’t do a lot of those with Stan. We did some, did some, but more it was like concert halls and theaters and stuff like that. So yeah, luckily I didn’t have too much of a bad time with those things with all the smoke coming. Of course I was a smoker back then too.
I was going to ask, and like you said how important lungs are to this whole affair that you do, so it’s pretty amazing that you could be a smoker and do that.

Okay well number one I didn’t smoke until I went in the Navy. So I was about 23 or 24 when I first started to smoke. And I smoked for quite a while and then I got a little — every once in a while when I’d go to take a good nice deep one I’d feel like a little zing. And I thought hmm, I think it’s trying to tell me something. So I quit smoking and that’s about 40 years ago now. And that went away but it scared me when I felt that little ping, right, like a sharp — I thought I’ve got to stop this. So I did and it paid off.
